cards.text: The war between the house of Saul and the house of David drags on, and on Saul's side, Abner keeps getting stronger. Abner is the commander of Saul's army, and he's the one who made Saul's son Ish-bosheth king (1 Samuel 14:50; 2 Samuel 2:8-9). Then Ish-bosheth accuses Abner of sleeping with Rizpah, his father Saul's concubine.

cards.question: Ish-bosheth just accused the man who made him king. How does Abner take it?

cards.text: Abner fires back, "Am I the head of a dog that belongs to Judah?" When a man opens with THAT, friend, buckle up for a SPEECH.

cards.question: In his speech, Abner brings up David. True or false: Abner tells Ish-bosheth he has already handed him over to David.

cards.text: Then Abner puts his own name on the line: "May God punish Abner, and ever so severely," if he doesn't do for David what the LORD has sworn to him.

cards.question: What does Abner swear he'll do for David?

answers.text: Bring the whole kingdom over to David
Split the land between both houses
Leave the war and go back home

cards.question: After Abner's oath, Ish-bosheth argues right back at him.

cards.text: For fear of Abner, Ish-bosheth doesn't dare say another word. That's the guy at work griping about the boss when the boss walks in, friend, and suddenly he's REAL interested in his own shoes.
So Abner sends messengers to David with a question, "To whom does the land belong?" and an offer. Friend, the commander of Saul's army just slid his résumé across the table to the OTHER side.

cards.question: Abner says his hand will be with David to bring all Israel over. What does Abner ask David to make with him?

cards.text: David says good, he'll make the covenant, but there's ONE thing he requires, and Abner better not show his face without it. David's working this door like a bouncer, friend: no it, no entry.

cards.question: What does David require Abner to bring when he comes to see him?

cards.text: Then David sends messengers straight to Ish-bosheth: "Give me back my wife, Michal," the bride David paid Saul's price for back in the day (1 Samuel 18:25-27).

cards.question: Ish-bosheth refuses David's demand and keeps Michal away from him.

cards.text: Ish-bosheth sends and takes Michal from her husband, Paltiel son of Laish. And Paltiel follows her, weeping all the way to Bahurim.

cards.question: Paltiel is still following Michal, weeping. True or false: David is the one who tells Paltiel to go back.

cards.text: Next, Abner sits down with the elders of Israel and tells them, "In the past you sought David as your king." Friend, the SAME man who made Ish-bosheth king is now pitching David like he's David's campaign manager.

cards.question: Abner tells the elders to take action now. What has the LORD said He will do through His servant David?

answers.text: Save Israel from the Philistines and all their enemies
Build a house for His name in Jerusalem
Lead Israel across the Jordan into a new land

cards.question: Abner doesn't stop with the elders. He also talks to Saul's own tribe (1 Samuel 9:1-2), the ___.

cards.text: Then Abner heads to Hebron with twenty of his men to tell David everything that seemed good to Israel and the whole house of Benjamin. Twenty men walking up to the other side's door in the middle of a WAR, and I get nervous ringing a doorbell to drop off a cookie box!

cards.question: Abner, the commander from Saul's side of the war, arrives at Hebron with twenty men. True or false: David holds a feast for them.
Abner tells David he'll go gather all Israel to make a covenant with him. So David sends Abner off, and Abner leaves Hebron in ___.

cards.text: That's this batch out of the oven for now. But friend, there are more trays coming, and you are going to want to see them.
